hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) can enhance drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction by generating hypotheses about potential binding affinities based on the underlying biochemical data, leveraging their ability to process and synthesize vast amounts of information from diverse sources. This hypothesis is supported by evidence that LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities in understanding complex relationships in data, as demonstrated in various studies [40], [41], [42], [43], and [44]. Furthermore, the integration of LLMs into DTI prediction frameworks can improve the accuracy of binding affinity predictions by utilizing advanced learning techniques that capture the nuances of protein-ligand interactions, as highlighted in recent research [46], [47], and [48].
